sourceIssues.printed: The Fourier expansion of T_ℓ on arbitrary Katz modular forms is written with every displayed sum starting at n≥1, without a cusp-form hypothesis.
sourceIssues.correction: Start those sums at n≥0 for general modular forms. For ℓ∤N the constant term is a₀(f)+ℓ^(k−1)a₀(⟨ℓ⟩f); for ℓ∣N it is a₀(f). Alternatively retain n≥1 and restrict to cusp forms or explicitly to positive-index coefficients.
sourceIssues.reason: Take N=1, residual characteristic 5, k=4 and ℓ=2. The integral level-one E₄ has q-expansion 1+240·Σ_(n≥1)σ₃(n)qⁿ, so its reduction has constant coefficient 1. The normalized two-isogeny formula is 2³f(q²)+(f(q^(1/2))+f(−q^(1/2)))/2; its constant coefficient is 8+1=9≡4 mod 5. Sums starting at n≥1 give zero. Positive-index coefficients and cuspidal comparisons are unaffected.
sourceIssues.known: new in this review; no correction was located in the checked primary listings. This finding concerns only the identified author copy; journal wording was unavailable.

interfaceChecks.name: level-problem-and-components
interfaceChecks.check: Use open H containing Γ(n); level one is H=GL₂(Ẑ). Honest full level 5 has four complex determinant components; fixed pairing selects one. Compare every component of the same algebraic object.

sources.match: For open H containing principal level, the compactified coarse curve is normal and projective with finite locally free j-map; its quotient and Katz–Mazur constructions agree. Full-level determinant labels are retained by the existing supplier, not replaced by fixed pairing.

interfaceChecks.name: existing-compactification-range
interfaceChecks.check: Reuse upstream Layer 10 only for prime N≥5 diamond quotients over ℤ[1/N]. A comparison candidate must be finite over the j-line, normal, and contain the common affine open schematically densely, with every component meeting it.

interfaceChecks.name: separate-base-change-claims
interfaceChecks.check: Coarse formation commutes with arbitrary base change over ℤ[1/gcd(6,n)]; smoothness holds over ℤ[1/n]. Thus n=5 permits all ℤ-bases, while n=4 excludes characteristic 2 from the general arbitrary-base-change claim. Neither statement says that relative normalization commutes with arbitrary base change.

sources.match: Smoothness holds after inverting n; arbitrary coarse-space base change holds after inverting gcd(6,n). Remark 6.6 excludes an unrestricted level-dividing characteristic-2 claim.

interfaceChecks.name: coarse-versus-stack
interfaceChecks.check: All integral Γ₀(N) cusps are regular, but this does not prove whole-fibre smoothness at a level-dividing prime. Naive and refined Γ₀ stacks have the same coarse curve; retain the refined stack for the boundary construction and check finite-flat descent separately.

sources.match: The Γ₀ coarse curve is regular away from the stated exceptional interior points, hence at every cusp; contraction from the naive to the refined stack induces an isomorphism of coarse spaces.
The compactified degeneracy maps of stacks are representable finite flat; the extended isogeny induces a map on invariant differentials.

interfaceChecks.name: boundary-map-and-differential
interfaceChecks.check: Compare both degeneracy maps on completed cusp rings and the invariant differential. A categorical map on coarse spaces does not itself transport the finite-flat stack trace.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.4.3 and boundary extension proof, pp.43–46
sources.match: The boundary extension uses quotient/contraction and Tate charts to extend the two stack maps and the isogeny differential; this is additional data beyond a categorical coarse map.

interfaceChecks.name: hecke-trace-scaling
interfaceChecks.check: The coherent pullback-isogeny-trace construction gives pT_p. Division by p requires the local integral theorem; Picard and étale push–pull use their own integral conventions. For a prime p∤N, weight 2 and positive index n≥1, the normalized coefficient is a_(np)(f)+p·a_(n/p)(⟨p⟩f), with the second term zero if p∤n. Example 4.5.3 proves this for Katz forms over an algebraic closure of characteristic r∤N, allowing p=r, by lifting to characteristic zero. For general modular forms include n=0 as in E115.

sources.locator: equation (4.5.1), p.46; Theorem 4.5.1, pp.46–47; Example 4.5.3, p.48
sources.match: The coherent composite equals pT_p, and its divisibility by p is proved locally. Example 4.5.3 gives the positive-index coefficients in residual characteristic prime to N; its n=0 omission for noncuspidal forms is E115.
